nodes.label: The Register (1493 entries, 165 to 1700)
nodes.rationale: The working record the five compendia are distilled from: it argues, reverses itself, and keeps the reversals. The compendia answer; the register is where the answers were got. An entry exists only because something rests on it.

nodes.label: The Eight Entry Kinds
nodes.rationale: finding 786, correction 367, measurement 296, prior art 65, new protocol 64, withdrawal 60, fault of mine 57, open question 28. The kinds deliberately overlap — counts are of entries matching each pattern, not a partition.

nodes.label: Load-Bearing Entries (376 cited by other entries)
nodes.rationale: Citation count is the register's own measure of what the record leans on: 1443 at 12x, 1460 at 10x, 1020/1576 at 7x, 784/1546 at 6x. 225 entries are cited in the book's chapters; the rest are the record of how the work went.

nodes.label: Four Kinds of Correction Resolution
nodes.rationale: A fault is only half an entry; what resolved it is the other half. The four resolutions are a published result, a measurement the work already held, an audit written after the fact, and the person's correction.

nodes.label: register_gen.py
nodes.rationale: Rebuild route: `python3 register_gen.py > REGISTER.md`. It reads the source, so the printed register cannot drift from it.

nodes.label: Lambda_spectra (spectral index)
nodes.rationale: The most worked index in the register. On (Z, c, l, 2S+1) it gives E = 1929; on (Ne, c) 1367; on (Ne, Z) 668; on (u, l, 2S+1) in eight bands, 9 — which exposed the neutral/ion discontinuity as a coordinate artefact.

nodes.label: Lambda_var (variable index)
nodes.rationale: Held charge as a coordinate before the brackets were built: every quantity relating the Rydberg electron to the nucleus is a nucleus-core quantity. The later fault a(period, block) rather than a(period, block, c) was a failure to read it.

nodes.label: Lambda_cross (crossing index)
nodes.rationale: Closes at E = 0 on (delta-n, l_g). Carries order, algebra (closed in Q(sqrt p) for p <= 7) and geometry but no analysis language — the half of the amplitude law that cannot be fitted and needs no fitting.

nodes.label: Lambda_descent (charge-descent index)
nodes.rationale: Closes at E = 0 on (c, regime). Has order and analysis both, and the statistics language answers yes for it and only for it — which is how the cypher located the boundary between the mathematics and the physics.

nodes.label: The Cypher (five languages over an index)
nodes.rationale: Asking which language falls silent is the diagnostic. It explained every fitting failure of the amplitude session: the fits were applied to the whole of a, half of which has no analysis language, so the constants kept absorbing each other.

nodes.label: E, the closure defect
nodes.rationale: E = 0 is the register's standing test of a closed index. Two cautions it records about itself: a closed sub-index says the roles are well-posed and nothing about whether the parent index wants them; and a low E can be binning rather than structure (E = 9 against a shuffle null of 15.0 +/- 1.9).

nodes.label: The operator R (alphabet recovery)
nodes.rationale: Because R recovers its alphabet, the ground set moves — which is why closure theorems quoted over a fixed ground set do not apply (entry 166). R does not enforce the singleton-output criterion.

nodes.label: The Corridor L(Z) < a < U(Z)
nodes.rationale: What survives after the law itself is withdrawn: 106 non-empty intervals with algebraic endpoints, any path through them reproducing the order. Its blind spot is occupancy — within one element all comparisons sit at one occupancy, so the corridor never saw the systematic that a_meas is too large.

nodes.label: The occupation law nu(n,l) = n − a·sqrt(n−l−1)
nodes.rationale: The electron enters the Pauli-admissible subshell of least nu; 106 of 106 elements admit such an a, on Pauli, the node count and the observed configurations alone — no spectroscopy. Deactivated as a law at register 1460 and retained as a FORM; held out it scores 90 of 106 against a Madelung null of 96.

nodes.label: The amplitude a(period, block, charge)
nodes.rationale: A single a serves no table; by (period, block) all eighteen cells are feasible and the output index closes at E = 0 in a box of 24, the six absent cells being exactly those the periodic table does not have. Charge was then forced in as a third argument — the ordering reverses completely across three charges at Ne = 20, a 17 eV swing.

nodes.label: The crossing value a_cross
nodes.rationale: a_cross = (n_r − n_g)/(sqrt p_r − sqrt p_g) is fixed by the subshell pair alone, independent of Ne and charge — proved by coincidence, since Ne = 56 and 70 share 6s/5d and share 1.2168 while crossing at different charges. 4s->3d at 1/sqrt3, 5s->4d at 1 exactly, 5d->4f at 1/sqrt2.

nodes.label: The charge descent of a
nodes.rationale: The charge at which a reaches the crossing is the physics; the crossing value is not. c = 2 is the only charge with two-sided brackets — every bracket is a lower bound at c = 1 and an upper bound at c = 3 — so the charge dependence is a descent passing through c = 2.

nodes.label: The node theorem p = n − l − 1
nodes.rationale: Unifying the radicand for any subshell, open or not, is what the candidacy correction bought; before it the radicand was defined only where a subshell begins.

nodes.label: Pauli admissibility (occ < 2(2l+1))
nodes.rationale: A fault of mine that reads as a physics law once stated properly: orthogonality (where a subshell begins) had been used as if it were admissibility, so at carbon the generator offered 3p where the electron enters the already-open 2p. Correcting it took the generator from 17.9% to 81.1%.

nodes.label: The Madelung order
nodes.rationale: Differs from the observed opening sequence at two of nineteen — La opens 5d at Z = 57 and Ac opens 6d at Z = 89 — which is exactly where every version of the filling generator failed. They were not equation failures: the equation was being asked to reproduce an order that is not the observed one.

nodes.label: The Janet (left-step) table
nodes.rationale: One of the register's standing index objects: closed, orientation cost zero, needing 35 cells for 120, and unreachable by brute force over the calendar (479,001,600 relabellings).

nodes.label: The periodic table is the law's index, not its output
nodes.rationale: 106 constants reduce to eighteen on (period, block), and the six infeasible cells are exactly the ones the table does not have. The inversion of the intended claim is the finding.

nodes.label: The observed ground configurations, read not computed
nodes.rationale: NIST ASD 5.12 GSIE, Z = 1 to 108, 108 of 108 electron counts validating. Every previous version built configurations by aufbau and patched exceptions by hand; that table was wrong at Pd and at Lr, and both were among the standing filling failures.

nodes.label: The reduced-mass Rydberg systematic (R_inf used where R_M is correct)
nodes.rationale: R_M = R_inf/(1 + m_e/M) understates every defect by n*(sqrt(R_inf/R_M) − 1). It explains He I's negative high-l defects exactly — not physics, the wrong constant — and the repair took three attempts because the constant must match the DATA's convention: R_M where levels are measured, R_inf where the table is a theoretical hydrogenic one.

nodes.label: The quantum defect delta
nodes.rationale: A Rydberg defect measures ONE electron outside a fixed core, which is why it cannot settle the 4s2/3d question — that is two electrons in the same shell. Low-n averages must exceed the asymptotic delta_0, and the register uses that direction as its literature check.

nodes.label: An integer object cannot be fitted and needs no fitting
nodes.rationale: A quantity that is ordinal, algebraic and geometric but not analytic is an integer object — here a finite set of nineteen surds with no derivative. Fitted parameters applied to it compete to represent surds, which is why they kept absorbing each other.

nodes.label: The singleton-output criterion
nodes.rationale: An index is closed when its output class is a singleton: two outputs mean the observer is still choosing which to read, and the choice is not in the object. Not enforced by R, which is why Lambda_var gave E = 0 both with delta alone and with n* added.

nodes.label: Zeno (one species per segment, checkpointed)
nodes.rationale: A segmentation discipline for long generated runs: the work is cut so each segment completes and checkpoints, so an interrupted run loses one species rather than the pass.

nodes.label: T8 — the series limit assignment
nodes.rationale: Generated rather than staged: store_gen.py gains limits(), assign_limit(), top_member_E() and MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.tsv gains six columns. The authored MEASUREMENTS.tsv is not rewritten, so the derivation is auditable against the authored record rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: The five limit statuses (parent-matched, forced, positional, unwitnessed, ion-derived)
nodes.rationale: Four statuses and no fifth until T8-J added ion-derived. No fallback replaces the one that was voided: where a parent's limit was never published the series cannot be defected, and unwitnessed is carried as a named bound — E measuring the world, not a gap to be filled.

nodes.label: T8-J — a J-resolved parent may borrow its limit from the parent ion's level table
nodes.rationale: limit(J) = printed limit(J0) + [E_ion(term,J) − E_ion(term,J0)]. Applied NARROW — the term's limit must be printed — because the same operation one step wider would absorb 145 old-void rows; a second data source per species is a ruling, not a regex.

nodes.label: §H.4 — history stands and the bridge says so
nodes.rationale: Where a document states a figure that was true when written and is now superseded, leave it and say so in the bridge. It holds evidence rather than deleting it, which is why authored stores are never rewritten and a superseded count is carried as named history.

nodes.label: §2.9 — the silent default is forbidden
nodes.rationale: A default written where a value is undefined impersonates a measurement. The jj rows' mult = 0 was therefore relabelled a null in a language that has no S — a relabel touching no coordinate of any index, rather than a deletion or a coercion.

nodes.label: The audit gate (25/25 · 6/6)
nodes.rationale: The register repeatedly records the gate passing over a fault: a vacuous test compares a list to itself, a COHERENCE audit passes because every target exists, and audits check consistency and not provenance. A can-fail simulation is therefore required of each widened check.

nodes.label: BOARD.md (the open-items board)
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt from the register at source rather than maintained by hand, because a board maintained separately drifts — it listed T2, T7 and T10 as open against entries recording them closed.

nodes.label: DIGEST.md (the session digest)
nodes.rationale: The standing rule that the opening turn reads the digest before stating work failed three sessions running — not for want of wording, but because the first message of a session arrives before the bank does. The recommendation is that the opening turn state nothing else until the upload lands.

nodes.label: LITERATURE.md (the standing literature record)
nodes.rationale: Holds four confirmations, two corrections, one exposure, one contested value, and the brackets searched for and NOT found. Where the literature disagrees with itself the compendium does not adjudicate — it records the disagreement and names the paper so anyone with access can finish the check.

nodes.label: COORDINATES.tsv (the index's cells)
nodes.rationale: 104,832 cells; 7,260 (Z, charge) pairs = 120·121/2 with charge 1…Z, l = 0–7 on every pair, E = 0 at Z = 120. mult is a fibration over N = Z − charge + 1, so a raw join/meet on 4-tuples measures the test and not the object.

nodes.label: MEASUREMENTS.tsv and MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.tsv
nodes.rationale: The authored store and its generated counterpart are kept as two files precisely so the derivation never overwrites the authored rows; every T8 residue lives in the value store and never in the coordinates.

nodes.label: store_gen.py
nodes.rationale: Closes the VALUE derivation but inherited its series list from the authored store — the first finding of the row-1 run was that no series constructor existed at all.

nodes.label: series_gen.py
nodes.rationale: Built on store_gen's own readers under the rules already on record rather than new ones, so the reconstruction is a check: 485 keys common, member counts 485/485, medians 351/351 agreeing, 0 disagreeing. Nothing was written to the store.

nodes.label: channels.py
nodes.rationale: The site of the Rydberg-constant systematic: it used R_inf for all species where the reduced-mass Rydberg is correct, affecting every one of 403 channels.

nodes.label: spectra.py
nodes.rationale: The median declaration was written into the generator rather than the generated file, so the roundtrip check carries it.

nodes.label: ground.py
nodes.rationale: Stores the observed ground configurations as read from NIST rather than as built by aufbau with hand-patched exceptions.

nodes.label: Angeli & Marinova, ADNDT 99 (2013) 69–95
nodes.rationale: Table of experimental nuclear ground-state charge radii: 909 isotopes of 92 elements, 1H to 96Cm. Its ceiling at Z = 96 is what bounds the A1 item.

nodes.label: Fricke & Heilig, Nuclear Charge Radii, Landolt-Börnstein I/20 (2004)
nodes.rationale: A different working group with a different method stopping at the identical Z = 96. Two independent evaluations with the same ceiling is not an editorial coincidence but the limit of what has been investigated.

nodes.label: Krug & von Lilienfeld, arXiv:2406.18416 (2024)
nodes.rationale: Alchemical insights into approximately quadratic energies of iso-electronic atoms: prior art for the quadratic in charge, tested over Z = 1–86 rather than four species. It saves three captures — what the six species add is a measured crossing, a datum and not a method.

nodes.label: Theodosiou, ADNDT 35, 473 (1986)
nodes.rationale: Source of the z >= 3 hydrogenic limit the high-charge slice extends to z ~ 90. Recorded as a bounded negative: paywalled at the publisher, request-only at the aggregator, no open PDF — a statement about that search rather than about the paper.

nodes.label: Bohr 1913 (R_inf -> R_M, after Fowler on the Pickering series)
nodes.rationale: The register's exemplar of a correction resolved by a published result: the reduced-mass correction was made in 1913 after Fowler objected that the Pickering series did not fit.

nodes.label: The Löwdin ordering (the many-electron quantity)
nodes.rationale: Sc I settles why no capture of Rydberg series can close the gap: the Löwdin ordering is a many-electron quantity and the compendium measures a one-electron one. Sc I has no 3d Rydberg series at all, 3d being a ground-configuration orbital there.

nodes.label: Slater screening (nu = n/Z_eff)
nodes.rationale: With no free parameter it threads the s-block and nothing else: 5 of 5 brackets at s, 1 of 5 at p, 0 of 1 at f. Twenty-one of twenty-five failures are the equation choosing p where the truth is d or f, because Slater under-screens d and f — which identifies exchange as the missing source cell by computation.

nodes.label: NIST ASD 5.12 / GSIE
nodes.rationale: The register's primary data source, read from disk rather than fetched; its own table conventions (series levels sitting beneath the limit they converge to; an ordinal letter naming a core term, not a second core) become named readings rather than assumptions.

nodes.label: The isoelectronic ladders (Ne = 20, 38, 56, 88)
nodes.rationale: A ladder constrains a only when delta-n != 0 — six of eleven are null for a reason the law supplies, and the earlier filter on closed shells was wrong. The six informative neutrals are all group 2, the only elements where 'an electron outside a closed core' is literally true.

nodes.label: A1 — the charge-radius anchors, bounded by measurement not access
nodes.rationale: Carried as an item waiting on a fetch when it is not one: four of six anchors are obtainable, and berkelium and californium do not exist as experimental values anywhere. Re-graded as a domain statement. The cost is asymmetric — californium, the richest anchor at three mass numbers, is one of the two that cannot be had.

nodes.label: Register 784 — a fault invisible to every audit
nodes.rationale: Invisible because audits check consistency and not provenance — the most-cited structural finding in the register.

nodes.label: Register 679 — the residual is structured
nodes.rationale: Li III's hydrogenic remainder is a measurement and not a rounding; it later turned out to be present in every channel rather than one.

nodes.label: Register 802 — monotonicity is directionally right and not universal
Register 868 — R_inf used where the reduced-mass Rydberg is correct
nodes.rationale: A systematic in every channel. Its companion finding is that He I cannot be corrected at all, because its levels were never preserved — a result kept without its inputs cannot be corrected when its method is.

nodes.label: Register 1460 — nu deactivated as a law, retained as a form
nodes.rationale: Second most-cited entry. The deactivation is why earlier entries about nu carry warnings: their content stands as facts about a form, not as statements about the periodic table.

nodes.label: Register 1475 / 1623 — space and time are columns, not indexes
nodes.rationale: The precedent that refuses T as an axis: a new measurement is a new coordinate and §18.4.1 does not admit one. T may enter the value store as a column; never as an axis.

nodes.label: Register 1306 — the observed ground configurations entry
Register 1318 — the cypher explains every fitting failure
The Kr I J = 0 metastable (a level defined by the absence of a transition)
nodes.rationale: Both failed attempts named a level that is already a J = 1 resonance — the pattern of failure is diagnostic. A level with no line to the ground state is hard to find in line-oriented sources, which is a reason to ask for a LEVEL table rather than a line list. Bounded from the four levels already held so the next attempt can be checked in one line.

hyperedges.label: The occupation law and everything it rests on
The cypher's split of a into crossing and descent
The T8 limit derivation, end to end
